name: Automate patient triage note entry
demonstrates: A nurse's triage-note workflow demonstrated once in a synthetic clinic app, compiled into a deterministic local program, and replayed with the note text as a parameter - including five injected fault classes that must halt instead of proceeding.

install.note: Installs the OpenAdapt launcher, compiler, and browser capability.

tryItCommand: openadapt flow replay bundle --param note="Triage note from $(date +%F)"

runStats.environment: MockMed synthetic clinic app (MIT, synthetic data only)
runStats.durationBasis: median of the three verified representative-run durations published in the pack outcomes (4820.51 ms, 4706.64 ms, 4697.14 ms)

provenance.label: Evidence pack manifest (byte inventory, SHA-256 bound)
Qualification report for the same pack

faq.question: Does this template make model calls when it runs?
faq.answer: No. Every one of the 18 published trials in evidence pack mockmed-triage-v3 recorded 0 model calls, including the 15 fault trials.

faq.question: What happens when the target is ambiguous?
faq.answer: The run halts before acting. In the published fault trials, an ambiguous locator produced a structural safety refusal - no action was admitted - in 3 of 3 trials.

faq.question: Is the clinical-write bundle certified?
faq.answer: No. The bundled tutorial is runnable but intentionally not certified for clinical writes; lint reports its unarmed irreversible final click and the strict policy gate refuses certification. That refusal is the safety boundary working.
